entry.title: Game of Phones: Harnessing Game Theory and LLMs in 'Bot Wars' to Counteract Phone Scams
entry.summary:
Phone scams impose substantial and growing costs on individuals and financial systems worldwide, yet existing countermeasures impose no resource cost on perpetrators. Strategic scam-baiting, in which automated agents engage scammers to deplete their operational capacity, offers a proactive alternative but requires dynamic strategy adaptation that static systems cannot provide. We introduce a game-theoretic framework enabling LLMs to learn effective counter-strategies through in-context experience without fine-tuning.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #llm

entry.title: The Covering Radius of $\text{RM}(1,9)$ is Precisely $242$
entry.summary:
Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Muller code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius, so that $\rho(1,n)$ is the largest possible nonlinearity of a Boolean function in $n$ variables. For odd $n$, the value of $\rho(1,n)$ was previously known only for $n\le 7$. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, but the exact determination of $\rho(1,9)$ has been a long-standing open question.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Optimal Threshold Implementations of all bijective 4-bit S-boxes and new Infinite Families
entry.summary:
Threshold implementations (TIs) are now an established class of side-channel countermeasures. Their underlying idea is simple and compelling: under mild, practical assumptions, they provide protection against glitches and allow composability. Yet our understanding of one-stage TIs with a minimal number of shares remains limited, both for cryptographically relevant families—particularly power functions—and for concrete small functions.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks
entry.summary:
Attack success rate (ASR) evaluates jailbreaks against large language models without accounting for repeated calls to the victim model. Yet each additional call gives the deployed system another opportunity to detect the attack and intervene. We introduce $\mathrm{ASR}_{\mathrm{STEP}}$, which penalizes additional victim-model calls while retaining binary success judgments.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #llm

entry.title: Auditor-Assisted Summary-Channel Verification for Hosted LLM Identity Substitution
entry.summary:
Hosted LLM services increasingly expose model identity as a product claim, but external users and auditors often cannot inspect which model configuration served a request. We study an auditor-assisted regime in which a trusted auditor enrolls claimed identities and prepares verification material before deployment, while audit-time verification uses only the claimed identity and released output, without runtime access to model internals, inference logs, routing decisions, or provider metadata. We propose SUMMARK, a summary-channel watermarking framework that uses user-visible reasoning summaries as a keyed audit surface.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #rust

entry.title: Binding Security of Combined KEMs: An Analysis of Real-World KEM Combiners. In this work we analyze the various binding properties of combiners for KEMs.
entry.summary:
In this work we analyze the various binding properties of combiners for KEMs. We show that several binding properties follow easily for the most general combiner—assuming a collision-resistant hash function—while more performance-oriented combiners require the respective property from one or both of the underlying KEMs. Other binding properties are not obtained as directly and require either more properties of one underlying KEM or the respective property from both KEMs.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
